hypothesis: There is a missing midpoint between '/refactor-subsystem extracts N files' and 'leave it bad': a single-file reorganizer that clusters symbols by domain, adds banner comments + a top-of-file index, declares __all__, and emits no semantic changes. Many 1K-LOC omnibuses are tolerable when sensibly organized; not all need extraction.

summary: Skill that takes an omnibus file as input and produces a structurally-reorganized version with: (1) symbol clustering by domain (reuse the same head-noun clustering /find-omnibus uses), (2) section banner comments grouping each cluster, (3) a top-of-file index/TOC docstring, (4) an explicit __all__ declaration listing the public API in order, (5) zero semantic changes. Default --require-recent-edits gate skips files with no edits in 90+ days unless --force ('leave stable files alone'). Outputs a --dry-run move plan first. Tooling caveat: a whole-file reorder buries git-blame trails — mitigated by 'git log --follow' / 'git blame -w -CC' which preserve authorship across moves; report should hint at these flags. Slots into the maintenance loop as a sibling to /refactor-subsystem: /find-omnibus → DECISION (decompose | reorganize | leave) → /refactor-subsystem OR /organize-file OR skip. Composes with: /propose-boundary (when reorg surfaces a clean seam, re-evaluate as a refactor candidate); the staged-boundary ADR (refuse-phasing rules apply if a reorg unexpectedly grows into a refactor).
title: /organize-file — reorganize an omnibus without restructuring

title: Conway's Law overlay — team-ownership boundaries as architecture force

hypothesis: Plan/spec/SKILL.md artifacts are DAGs flattened into numbered lists; the list hides the dependency structure (permitting silent inconsistency) and the parallelism (hiding the critical path). Declaring each stage's inputs and outputs as an explicit graph yields both consistency-checking and critical-path scheduling from one representation. Open question: authoring cost, and whether the graph is hand-authored or inferred from existing stage headings.
summary: Plan, spec, and SKILL.md artifacts are dependency graphs flattened into numbered lists. The list format hides which steps actually depend on which — permitting silent inconsistency (a step consuming an input nothing upstream produced) and hiding what is parallelizable versus on the critical path. Proposal: each stage declares its inputs and outputs so the artifact carries an explicit stage-IO graph. One representation pays twice — it can be mechanically checked (the IO graph must close) and scheduled (critical path = longest dependency chain; everything off it parallelizes). Surfaced by dogfooding this ecosystem's own process: the WS1-WS4 plan run this session presented four workstreams as sequential 1-2-3-4 when WS1/WS2/WS4 were nearly independent, and stated a guessed disposition for specs.py as fact because the prose had no slot to mark that it depended on an upstream scout verdict (which later contradicted it). plan-phased-refactor-skill is the narrow instance — a phase-graph for one boundary refactor; this is the general principle under it. Feeds the instruction-artifact coherence detector: the IO-closure check is only possible once the graph is declared.
title: Dependency-explicit plan and skill artifacts — declare the stage-IO graph, not a numbered list

hypothesis: A SKILL.md / plan / spec is an executable spec written in English with no compiler or test suite to punish internal contradiction. Its coherence is checkable structurally — frontmatter vs body, stage-IO graph closure, reference resolution — with no semantic NLP. Open question: what fraction of real incoherence is structurally detectable versus needs human judgment.
summary: All nine architectural smells in the catalog target host code; none targets the ecosystem's own instruction artifacts — SKILL.md, plans, specs, ADR bodies. Yet those are executable specs written in English, with no compiler or test suite to punish internal contradiction, so they drift freely. Evidence this is a real defect class: this session's framework:django mislabels on map-subsystem and find-omnibus were exactly 'frontmatter claims X, body claims not-X' — find-omnibus's own Scope section states it does not touch Django — and nothing in the catalog would catch it (find-rule-surface-drift checks the doc table against the filesystem, find-comment-drift checks comments against code; neither checks a skill artifact against itself). Proposal: a SUSPECT detector — candidate smell 10 — checking instruction artifacts for structural coherence: frontmatter agrees with body, every stage consumes only inputs produced upstream (the stage-IO graph closes), every referenced skill/file/path resolves, claims stated as fact versus assumption are distinguished. Deliberately structural, not semantic — no NLP, no 'understand causal flow'; give prose a type-checker, not a brain. decisions.py audit/link-check — a working consistency checker for ADRs, wired into CI this session — is the proven prototype to generalize. Instruction-artifact analog of system-coherence-drift-detector (which does the same at the code level). Depends on dependency-explicit-artifacts for the stage-IO-closure check.
title: Instruction-artifact coherence detector (smell 10) — a SUSPECT pass for the ecosystem's own SKILL.md / plan / spec prose

hypothesis: Code is reconciled, not derived: the docs-to-code transform is a relation, so the graph can propagate dirtiness deterministically but cannot regenerate content. Open question — what fraction of reconciliation is safely automatable as detect-and-propose versus needs gated human acceptance.
summary: Model the project as a typed DAG so a change reveals everything it affects, including docs. Three node tiers: source (ADRs, rules, style guides, hand-written subsystem docs — authored, never regenerated); derived docs (indexes, catalogs, dashboards — pure functions of their inputs, regenerate freely, the dashboard.md regen already works this way); reconciled (code, and SKILL.md prose). Authority is one-way (docs win as intent) but generation is not — code cannot be re-rendered from docs because the docs-to-code transform is a relation not a function, and code accumulates underdetermined decisions docs never captured. The graph therefore propagates typed dirtiness, not content: changing a style guide marks dependents style-dirty but requirements-clean, scoping and cost-routing each reconciliation. Reconciliation is build-system-style invalidate-then-rebuild where rebuild is LLM-or-human judgment, not a deterministic compile. Code-to-docs is covered by decision-extraction/case-law as a promotion — lifting an implicit decision to an explicit source node, React's lift-state-up move — which keeps the graph acyclic. Passive v0 is near-term and cheap: extract edges that already exist (Python imports for code-to-code; ADR applies_to for rule-to-file, which decisions.py link-check already parses and validates) into one queryable place, mark dirty, show blast radius. The active reconciliation engine is the genuine future undertaking and is model-dependent. Feasible now only because LLM labor removes the human doc-rot failure that always killed doc-driven systems; but automatic must mean detect-and-propose, never auto-apply, since auto-applying many LLM rewrites unsupervised rebuilds the vibe-coded disaster at machine speed. Generalizes dependency-explicit-artifacts from within-artifact stage-IO to across-artifact doc-to-code dependencies.
title: Docs-to-code dependency graph — typed DAG with one-way authority and dirtiness propagation

hypothesis: The comprehension tax is dominated by cacheable components (repo-shape and file-digest), so caching the MAP artifact recovers most of it with no context-rot cost; batching only helps the fix stage, only behind characterization tests, and only within a model-dependent budget calibrated by differential testing against the separated baseline.
summary: A planner that compiles an optimal execution plan for a set of skill invocations, attacking the comprehension tax — the repeated cost of re-establishing repo and file understanding once per skill per file, which was the real time sink in this ecosystem's multi-week build. Decompose the tax into four parts: repo-shape and file-digest are cacheable (the MAP-tier artifact is the natural cache); cross-finding synthesis is currently performed by no skill (the orchestrator does it by hand); fix-context blast-radius is irreducible. Lever priority: first cache shared comprehension (MAP as a required input, not an optional doc), then parallelize detection into clean windows, and only last batch fixes — the smallest and riskiest win. Detection and fixing have opposite batching profiles: detection is independent and should be parallelized (clean context per scout, which is anti-context-rot), fixing is interacting and must share one context but only behind characterization tests, within a context-rot budget that behaves like a scheduler issue width. Tests are externalized comprehension — they let the model forget, which is what makes a fix batch fit in a window. Run regimes differ: iterative (pre-commit or PR, diff-scoped — the SUSPECT tier is not yet diff-scoped, a real gap), major (full-system analysis, MAP tier), and merge (an iterative run plus cross-branch artifact-staleness detection). The separated dev bundle is both the compiler source and the test oracle: differential-test the batched distribution bundle against it the way -O2 output is tested against -O0; the distribution bundle is compiled for a target model, since safe batch width is model-dependent and must be calibrated, not guessed. The planner also absorbs cross-finding synthesis post-run. Endorsed in conversation as a good idea.
title: Skill-execution planner — a scheduler over the skill graph that reduces the comprehension tax

hypothesis: Comprehension-tax component one — per-skill repo-shape re-derivation — dominates total run cost; an enriched ledger carrying cost fields can confirm or refute this, turning a current guess into a measurement.
summary: Today reports/_meta/effectiveness.jsonl records per-run counts only (findings_total and buckets). Enrich the schema to retain per-finding traces — code excerpt, detector output, scout rationale, and the verified label including hard negatives — plus cost fields (tokens, wall-clock, context size at decision points). One small change to an artifact that already exists, with three payoffs: it makes the comprehension tax measurable instead of anecdotal; it supplies the calibration data the skill-execution-planner needs to fit safe per-model batch budgets; and it becomes a synthetic-data corpus of verified architectural-judgment traces with hard negatives — the rare and valuable kind of training data, unlike generated code which is worthless because the internet is already saturated with it. Concrete evidence the value is currently discarded: the find-omnibus scan scan-20260516-020044 produced four training-grade hard negatives (the facets_not_domains bucket — product_topology.py and three detector files, each with a facet-vs-domain rationale explaining why it looks like an omnibus but is not), and the ledger kept only the bucket count, not the rationale. This is the smallest and most concrete of the three linked intakes and the right near-term first step.
title: Verified-judgment-trace ledger — enrich effectiveness.jsonl from a per-run tally to a per-finding corpus

The useful lesson from dogfooding was that performance scanners need conservative receiver heuristics and measurement-first recommendations so they generate leads rather than confident rewrites.

hypothesis: Context-composition and side-effect/blast-radius analysis are two query directions over one typed, weighted, two-speed project knowledge graph; building that graph as an always-derived first-class substrate lets the quality skills become queries instead of scanners, and lets an agent classify task triviality (= bounded blast radius) instead of defensively over-engineering.
summary: Captures where the code-quality skill ecosystem should converge: an always-current, easy-to-parse, typed-and-weighted project knowledge graph as the shared substrate. Core thesis from a design conversation. (1) The two long-standing branches are the same datastore viewed from two directions: branch 1 (reduce the exploration needed to be sure of context) is a backward-plus-neighborhood walk from a task seed; branch 2 (be sure of the magnitude of a change side-effects) is a forward walk from the same seed. One graph, two traversals. (2) Triviality classification falls out for free: trivial means bounded blast radius, so an agent cannot safely call a task trivial without branch 2 — the over-engineering failure mode (the Claude-vs-Codex meme) is the rational behavior of an agent that cannot see the boundary of its own certainty. (3) Graph design: nodes are symbols, files, models, routes, tasks, contracts, domain terms, ADRs, tests, known-issues; edges are typed and layered by automatability — static edges (calls, imports, refs) are auto-derived and genuinely always-current; dynamic/registry edges (Celery dispatch-by-name, URL conf, signals, template-context) are dynamic in general but enumerable per project and declared; semantic/contract edges (must-stay-format-equivalent, serialized-into-export) and state edges (a computation change retroactively reinterprets persisted rows, the hardest class, almost nothing catches it) must be declared and accreted on surprise. (4) The honest tool output is the boundary between what the graph is sure of and what it is not, not a false-precise list of exact side-effects — and that boundary is what removes the incentive to over-engineer. (5) Two-speed freshness: always-up-to-date is honest only for the auto layer; declared layers carry per-edge provenance, confidence, and staleness markers, because a confident-looking graph that is actually guessing is worse than no graph. (6) Edges are weighted as well as typed — risk-weighting is what turns a 40-hit dump into one ranked answer, the way a senior engineer checks the 2 dangerous edges and ignores 38. (7) The reframe for the skill ecosystem: skills stop being scanners that re-derive structure and emit stale reports, and become queries and interpreters over the graph — MAP is a rendered view, SUSPECT is a graph predicate, EXPLAIN renders subgraph-plus-semantics, REFACTOR is a graph diff, GUARD is a graph invariant. Five verbs, one substrate. (8) Anti-rot discipline: derive what you can so it cannot drift from code; co-locate the declared edges next to the code they describe (a contract annotation by the function) rather than centralizing them into a new rot magnet. (9) Easy-to-parse is load-bearing, not cosmetic: a boring universal queryable format makes the graph infrastructure (PR review becomes a before/after graph diff, onboarding and the subsystem atlas become renders, health metrics become queries); a bespoke store makes it a silo. (10) Migration trigger from the current markdown-shard era (ADRs, precedents.yml, known-issues.md, find-* reports, CONTEXT.md, importance-map.md — the correct early prototype): migrate to a real store when agents start failing to join across the shards, i.e. when manual cross-referencing cost exceeds the cost of paying for the store once. Closely related to docs-to-code-dependency-graph (the docs-to-code slice of the same graph, with dirtiness propagation) and skill-execution-planner (the graph is the comprehension-tax cache that planner needs).
title: Code knowledge graph as the convergence substrate for the quality skills

hypothesis: Making the target architecture an explicit, drift-checkable artifact lets the existing incremental tiers be aimed: re-architecting becomes accumulable rather than one high-risk transform, and behavior-preserving refactors stop polishing a system inside an expired frame.
summary: The ecosystem has durable artifacts for point decisions (ADRs), for features (specs), and for CURRENT state (map-subsystem, the map-project atlas, importance-map) — but nothing holds DESIRED whole-system state. The target architecture lives only in a human head, which is why behavior-preserving refactors can only rearrange furniture inside the founding frame and can never aim at a better one (the conversation phrase: software does not rot, it outlives its founding frame). Proposal: a standing, durable target-architecture artifact (Shape B) — a sibling to the current-state atlas — plus a drift metric defined as diff(current atlas, Shape B), computable as a query once the knowledge-graph index exists. Effect: re-architecting stops being a single high-risk transform and becomes a direction that many safe small moves (the refactor tier, the System-tier chain, /decide) accumulate toward, each scored by whether it reduces drift. Distinct from propose-architecture-skill, which generates a one-shot proposal — this idea PERSISTS the chosen target and measures distance to it continuously, and propose-architecture output is the natural seed for authoring the artifact. Distinct from system-coherence-drift-detector, which measures intrinsic coherence rather than distance from a declared target. Distinct from map-project, which captures current state only. Scoped but parked: worth exploring, no build slot yet; the index keystone (code-knowledge-graph-substrate) should land first.
title: Target-architecture artifact — persist desired Shape B plus a drift metric the incremental tiers aim at

summary: Sequencing note from a design conversation (host project host-a). Of the convergence ideas, the derived knowledge-graph index is the keystone and should be built first, deliberately conservatively: keep the markdown/JSONL/YAML shards (ADRs, precedents.yml, known-issues, find-* reports, CONTEXT.md, importance-map, the idea ledger) as the git-diffable human-readable source of truth, and add the index only as a disposable derived cache rebuilt from those shards. SQLite with recursive CTEs is almost certainly enough for the dependency-graph traversals — a bespoke graph DB is not warranted yet and would trade away the shard-level diffability that is the ecosystem ethos. Keystone argument: churn detection, per-idea coverage audits, and target-architecture drift measurement each otherwise re-derive the same cross-shard joins by hand on every run, so one index pays for itself across all three. New framing the conversation added: even with flat files retained, specialized query and update tooling over them is itself the deliverable — the mental transform of a shard into a usable frame is a comprehension tax, and that tax is a direct cause of AI-agent failure, disproportionately so in high-velocity vibe coding where no human rechecks the details, so the index is a correctness and safety surface, not merely a speed optimization. Broader intent: candidate to productize for people doing too much vibe coding; the index is the load-bearing piece of any such product and will need real optimization work. Pairs with the new target-architecture-artifact intake — drift is a query over this index.

Back-link to target-architecture-artifact (the drift-metric idea is a query over this index). Reverse of the edge recorded on that intake; the earlier dev-note event passed --edges-added but the dev-note kind does not apply edges, so this edge event records it properly.

Addendum — the authority-gradient framing. docs-to-code is the ideal case not because traversal is one-way (side-effect analysis always needs both directions plus sibling expansion) but because every edge carries a designated authority side: the doc declares intent, the code conforms. That single property buys monotone one-way dirtiness propagation, near-statically-declared edges, and — the crux — findings that are actionable rather than merely alarming. An edge with an authority label yields an answer (code B violated contract C); an edge without one yields only a question (A and B diverged — which is wrong?). The dangerous edges in the general code graph (format-equivalent peer writers, ordering assumptions) are dangerous precisely because they are directionless: no designated authority. Key reframe: the messy code graph is not a different graph from docs-to-code — it is the same graph before its implicit peer-couplings have been promoted to authored contracts. Contract extraction (what the refactor skills already do) is exactly the operation that converts one undirected high-risk edge into two clean docs-to-code edges, by introducing an authority node both sides derive from. So docs-to-code-dependency-graph is not a sibling idea but a BAND of this substrate — the subset of edges that already have a clean authority gradient; the substrate is the whole graph including the not-yet-authoritative edges. This yields a concrete architectural health metric instead of a vibe: the fraction of risky coupling that has a designated authority. A codebase where every dangerous edge is authority-labelled has cheap freshness and answerable side-effects; one full of directionless peer edges makes every change a guess (the over-engineering failure mode, structurally). The graph measures that fraction; the maintenance loop's job is to raise it — push high-risk coupling from the undirected end toward the directed-authoritative end. Implication for reconciling the two ledger entries: treat docs-to-code-dependency-graph as the directed-authoritative band of code-knowledge-graph-substrate, not a separate artifact.

hypothesis: Dismissals fingerprinted on the offending code region (normalized AST node plus the evidence set the finding cited) expire on code-region change rather than elapsed time, so a finding only re-surfaces when the structure it accused has actually moved. Open questions: (a) what AST normalization level keeps re-surface rate near zero on reformat/rename while still catching real edits; (b) whether the evidence-set hash should be conjunctive (finding re-surfaces when any cited input changes) or disjunctive (only when the AST node changes); (c) how to handle scattered-concept findings that have no single node — likely fingerprint the union of cited sites, re-surface on any union member changing.
summary: Without a dismissal-memory layer, every SUSPECT skill (find-omnibus, find-implicit-state, find-complexity-hotspots, the proposed find-scattered-concept, etc.) re-emits the same known-fine findings on every run — turning the scanner from a signal into noise the moment the project has any non-trivial accumulated review history. The dismissal layer needs three properties to be useful: (1) persistence per finding-identity, not per scan; (2) selective re-surface when the underlying code-region changes, not when the calendar advances — directly analogous to the stale-detection principle in host-a (stale = no progress increment, not elapsed time); (3) survives reformat, rename, and movement that don't change semantics. The hard sub-problem is fingerprint granularity. Too coarse (file path + finding-type) re-surfaces on any unrelated edit to the file, defeating the dismissal. Too fine (exact line range + character offsets) re-surfaces on a single space change. Plausible right grain: a tuple of (finding-type, normalized-AST-node-hash for the offending node, content-hash of the evidence set the finding cited) — so a dismissal survives unrelated edits but invalidates when the accused structure or its supporting evidence changes. Mechanics: the ledger lives under .claude/quality/dismissals.jsonl (sibling to findings.jsonl in host-a), keyed by fingerprint, with reviewer, rationale, and the original finding payload preserved for audit. SUSPECT skills query the ledger after producing findings and filter dismissed entries from the user-facing report while surfacing a count and a 'show suppressed' flag. Dismissal is a first-class GUARD output — the human review step of any SUSPECT report. Open design choices to investigate during build: rationale taxonomy (false-positive / accepted-debt / intentional-deviation / superseded), expiry escape valves (force re-review after N months for accepted-debt vs never for intentional-deviation), and whether dismissals propagate across forks/branches via git or stay per-checkout. Composes with every find-* SUSPECT skill in the ecosystem; once the code-knowledge-graph substrate exists, the AST-node-hash component should be derived from the graph rather than recomputed per skill. Surfaced during host-a maintainability experiments session (2026-05-19) as the missing piece that lets SUSPECT skills graduate from one-shot scans to standing fitness functions.

summary:
Full substrate design captured during host-a maintainability-experiments arc (2026-05-19), preserved here before pivoting to a lean cut that defers most of this build.

Schema (10 node tables): files, symbols, models, routes, tasks, contracts, domain_terms, adrs, tests, lint_rules. Two-speed freshness: last_seen_at always-updated by importers; last_verified_at only on declared/contract layers, hand-bumped on review.

Edge taxonomy (18 edges across 4 authority layers):
- Layer 1 (static auto-derived, freshness honest): imports, calls, model_fk, model_inheritance, type_annotation_uses.
- Layer 2 (dynamic registry, per-project enumerable): celery_dispatch_by_name, url_resolves, signal_send, signal_receive, template_context_provides, template_context_uses.
- Layer 3 (test linkage, auto-derivable from coverage): test_covers, test_setup_uses.
- Layer 4 (declared semantic/contract/state, accreted on surprise): must_stay_format_equivalent, serialized_into_export, retroactively_reinterprets_persisted, contract_exports, contract_requires.

The authority-gradient framing carries through: every Layer-4 edge has a designated authority side (the contract declares intent, code conforms). Layer-1 edges are directionless but auto-fresh. The maintenance loop's job is to push high-risk Layer-1 couplings into Layer-4 by extracting contracts — converting one undirected edge into two clean authority-labelled edges.

AST normalization v1 (aggressive) for symbol-level fingerprints used by the dismissal layer and by node-identity in the graph: strip local + parameter names to LOCAL_n / PARAM_n with stable ordering; keep module-level names, call targets, string literals, decorators, attribute-access chains, and type annotations; drop docstrings, comments, whitespace; SHA256 the canonicalised AST text and truncate to the first 16 hex chars. Calibration target ≥80% correlation against human-labelled semantic-vs-cosmetic on 20 historical commits.

Build phases as originally planned (5 weeks @ ~15h/week, ~3000 LOC):
- Phase 1 (inventories — DONE under .claude/tasks/maintainability-experiments/07 and 08; the planned 09 engineering-skills-2-overlap was rolled into the lean-cut plan directly).
- Phase 2: SQLite store, 14 importers (one per node table plus key edge classes), recursive-CTE traversal predicates, health metric (fraction of risky coupling with designated authority).
- Phase 3: per-subsystem contract YAMLs (see new subsystem-contract-artifact intake), 5 pilot contracts, conscious-change loop (contract bump → dependents review-due via cross-shard query), lint-integration via enforced_by: lint:<rule>.
- Phase 4: scanner-to-query rewrites for /find-dormant, /map-subsystem, /architecture-fit; reports/_meta/graph-dashboard.md; graph.py query --format dot visualisation.

4-lane validation strategy: Lane A real-traffic dogfood (≥5 dismissals across SUSPECT skills, FP resurface rate ≤10%); Lane B backtest harness (100-commit replay, contract injection, noqa-stratified ground truth); Lane C AST-normalisation calibration (semantic-vs-cosmetic correlation on 20 historical commits); Lane D scanner-vs-substrate parity (rewritten scanners must produce supersets of the markdown-shard outputs, not different sets).

Decide-gate framework: explicit kill/adapt/keep criteria at each phase exit. Kill triggers retire the deferred intakes with retrospective notes; adapt keeps the substrate but rescopes (e.g. drop dynamic-registry layer 2 if importer cost exceeds payoff); keep is the only state that unlocks the next phase.

Lean-cut decision (2026-05-19): user chose Option B (full substrate) primarily out of loss aversion — not wanting deferred pieces to get forgotten. The engineering-skills-2 ledger is the recoverable place to park those pieces, so the right plan was a ~1.5-week three-track cut: AST-fingerprinted dismissal ledger (Track 1, in-flight under false-positive-dismissal-ledger), concept-glossary + drift audit (Track 2, addresses the _field_guidance divergence failure mode without the full substrate), consolidated findings-and-dispositions report (Track 3). See feedback-loss-aversion-in-option-selection memory for the pattern.

Revisit-when triggers for promoting this substrate back to in-flight: (a) 3+ SUSPECT skills independently need cross-cutting queries the markdown shards can't answer; (b) concept-drift audit (Track 2 lean-cut deliverable) hits >3 cases/quarter that lints don't catch; (c) the directed-authoritative band (docs-to-code-dependency-graph) is built first and proves the authority-gradient framing on a small slice.

Related intakes: docs-to-code-dependency-graph (directed-authoritative band of this same graph, lower-risk first slice), target-architecture-artifact (drift metric as a query over this index), subsystem-contract-artifact (the Layer-4 declared-edge surface), false-positive-dismissal-ledger (the dismissal layer that should consume AST-node-hash from the graph once it exists).

Greenlighted as Track 1 of the host-a maintainability lean cut (2026-05-19). Pieces being built in host-a: scripts/_lib/ast_normalize.py (~150 LOC, extends scripts/chunk_file.py's tree walker), scripts/dismissals.py CLI (~150 LOC, mirroring scripts/quality_findings.py's discipline), .claude/quality/dismissals.jsonl append-only ledger. Pilot consumer: /find-implicit-state (highest false-positive rate per inventory 08). Week-1 decide gate: ≥5 real dismissals dogfooded via CLI with rationales, FP resurface rate ≤10% on cosmetic edits, AST-normalisation calibration ≥80% correlation vs human-labelled semantic-vs-cosmetic on 20 historical commits. Graceful kill path: if calibration <80% after one tune-and-retest cycle, drop the dismissal track and salvage ast_normalize.py as a standalone library — the filter-dismissed wiring is designed to degrade to passthrough when ledger is missing or malformed, so the kill is reversible and non-destructive.

Implementation design for the lean-cut build of this layer.

AST normalisation v1 (aggressive): strip local + parameter names to LOCAL_n / PARAM_n with stable ordering; keep module-level names, call targets, string literals, decorators, attribute-access chains, and type annotations; drop docstrings, comments, whitespace; SHA256 the canonicalised AST text and truncate to the first 16 hex chars. This level of aggression intentionally tolerates rename inside a function (because most cosmetic edits do not change semantics) at the cost of missing rare cases where local-variable identity is load-bearing — calibration measures that tradeoff.

Record schema: a dismissal opens with record_kind: finding plus code_region containing ast_node_hash + evidence_set_hash; subsequent records mutate state via record_kind: event with event_kind in {invalidated, revalidated, withdrawn, expired, scope_changed, human_acked}. Append-only; no in-place mutation. Mirrors the event-history shape of .claude/quality/findings.jsonl in host-a.

CLI verbs (mirror scripts/quality_findings.py): add, list, withdraw, renew, validate, check, filter-dismissed. filter-dismissed is the integration point: SUSPECT-skill reports are piped through it, dismissed findings are stripped (with a count and a 'show suppressed' affordance), and the filter degrades to passthrough on missing/malformed ledger. .pre-commit-config.yaml gets an advisory dismissal-ledger-format JSONL-schema check — non-blocking, surfaces drift without failing the lane.

Adversarial-review mitigations baked into the lean cut:
- Calibration moves before authoring (Week-1 step 1). If <80% correlation after one tune cycle, the track dies cheaply.
- filter-dismissed always returns the input set when index/ledger is absent or malformed. Failures degrade to current behavior, not worse.
- Pre-commit hook is advisory only — never blocks a commit on dismissal-ledger format errors.
- Dogfood target ≥10 dismissals by end of Week 2 (Track-3 fix-now dismissals count toward the threshold), to avoid optimistic conclusions from a 5-sample base.
- Pilot choice (/find-implicit-state) was selected because it has the highest FP rate per inventory 08 — concentrates signal where validation matters most.
- Long-run: once code-knowledge-graph-substrate is built, the AST-node-hash component derives from the graph instead of being recomputed per skill, removing one duplicated implementation.

Open design choices to settle during build: rationale taxonomy (false-positive / accepted-debt / intentional-deviation / superseded); whether intentional-deviation dismissals are immortal or carry a force-review-after-N-months timer (lean-cut default: immortal, revisit on demand); whether dismissals propagate via git (lean-cut default: yes, the JSONL is checked in alongside findings.jsonl) or stay per-checkout.

hypothesis: Per-subsystem contract YAMLs declared next to the subsystem code (exports / requires / concept_refs / promises) give boundary lints an explicit, accreted authority side for what is currently implicit peer coupling — converting the directionless-peer-edges band of the code graph into the docs-to-code authority-labelled band one boundary at a time. With concept_ref pointers to a shared concepts.yaml glossary and lint-integration via enforced_by: lint:<rule>, each existing boundary lint becomes the enforcement mechanism for a contract violation rather than a free-standing rule with no anchor. A conscious-change loop (contract version bump → dependents marked review-due) replaces 'audit before merge' with 'audit before publish'. Open questions: (a) what fraction of host-a's 15+ boundary lints can be re-anchored without rewriting; (b) whether contract version bumps need semantic-vs-cosmetic distinction the way commit history does; (c) whether the conscious-change loop fires usefully without the graph substrate underneath (lean cut grep over requires: blocks vs full graph query); (d) which subsystem coupling has the highest cost and lowest current lint coverage — candidate is the export schema ↔ FlattenedData ↔ WWS Items chain (format-equivalence drift between parallel writers, smell 5 in architectural-smells.md).
summary:
Captures the deferred contract-artifact track from the host-a maintainability lean cut (2026-05-19). The lean cut ships only the companion .claude/contracts/concepts.yaml glossary plus a one-off /find-concept-divergence scanner; this intake preserves the full contract-format design for whenever the revisit-when triggers fire.

YAML schema: id, version, status, title, date, applies_to (path globs), exports, requires (each with concept_ref pointer), concept_refs (canonical glossary slugs), promises (semantic invariants beyond the type signature), provenance (which ADR / lint / canonical-patterns row this contract anchors), exceptions (path allowlist with rationale, mirroring no-retailer-references). Stored at .claude/contracts/<subsystem>.yaml — co-located near the subsystem code, not centralised into a new rot magnet (anti-rot discipline carried over from the code-knowledge-graph-substrate intake).

Companion glossary: .claude/contracts/concepts.yaml (the lean cut builds this surface now). Each entry: name, aliases, definition, superseded_by (for rename safety like retailer→site per ADR 0012). All contract concept_refs resolve into this single glossary, so renames cascade through the graph by editing one node.

Conscious-change loop: contract version bump triggers dependents review-due via a cross-shard query. Pre-substrate fallback: a grep over requires: blocks in sibling contracts. Post-substrate: a graph query over Layer-4 contract_requires edges. Either way, the contract is the authority — the lint is the enforcement mechanism, not the source of truth.

Lint integration scheme: each existing boundary lint gets enforced_by: lint:<rule> annotation inside the matching contract. The contract owns the intent; the lint owns the check. This breaks the current pattern where 15+ host-a lints are free-standing rules with no anchor a non-host-a reader can recover from.

5 pilot contract drafts (sketched during planning):
1. site-intelligence-readonly — the sidecar must not write to Django ORM. enforced_by: lint:site-intelligence-boundary. concept_refs: site-intelligence-sidecar, django-orm. exceptions: explicit write-back queue endpoints documented in site-intelligence-sidecar.md.
2. safe-dispatch — celery task dispatch must use safe_dispatch wrapper (no bare .delay across boundaries). enforced_by: lint:safe-dispatch. concept_refs: celery-wire-name, safe-dispatch-pattern.
3. core-wire-name-preservation — celery task names are wire-stable contracts; renames require versioning + rollover. enforced_by: lint:no-task-rename. concept_refs: celery-wire-name, task-identity. provenance: ADR 0007.
4. textchoices-state — string status comparisons forbidden against TextChoices fields. enforced_by: lint:stringly-status. concept_refs: textchoices-state, job-status.
5. retailer-to-site-renamed — Retailer* identifiers superseded by Site* outside the allowlist. enforced_by: lint:no-retailer-references. concept_refs: retailer (superseded_by: site). provenance: ADRs 0011, 0012, 0014. exceptions: migrations, ADRs 0007/0011/0012, tools/rename/.

6th pilot question raised by adversarial review (no lint enforcement yet): the export schema ↔ FlattenedData ↔ WWS Items chain — parallel-writer format-equivalence drift, the canonical example of smell 5 in architectural-smells.md. A contract here would be load-bearing precisely because no lint catches it today. If the contract format is going to add real value beyond re-anchoring existing lints, this is where it shows up first.

Revisit-when triggers for promotion to in-flight: (a) concept-drift audit (lean Track 2 deliverable) hits >3 cases/quarter that lints don't catch; (b) a mid-sized refactor breaks an implicit subsystem boundary twice (signal that implicit-peer coupling has become a tax); (c) code-knowledge-graph-substrate is built (contracts become real Layer-4 edges rather than YAML files with grep-based dependents).

Comparison to existing artifacts: precedents.yml is implementation case-law (exemplar-driven, recurring mechanism, scoped to one decision); subsystem contracts are subsystem-scoped boundary declarations (exports/requires-driven, scoped to one subsystem). Different unit of analysis, both layered onto the same code, both queryable by the future graph substrate. ADRs are decisions at a point in time; contracts are durable subsystem-interface declarations that ADRs anchor into. CONTEXT.md Language section is the human-readable mirror of concepts.yaml (the lean cut adds a header pointer between them).

Migration path: (Phase A) lean cut ships concepts.yaml + find-concept-divergence scanner — done as Track 2 of the host-a lean cut. (Phase B) draft pilot 1 (site-intelligence-readonly) as a single contract file, validate the schema against one real subsystem before generalising. (Phase C) generalise to pilots 2–5 + add the bump-triggers-review loop. (Phase D) once code-knowledge-graph-substrate is built, absorb concept_refs and contract_requires as real graph edge types and retire the grep-based fallback.

Composes with code-knowledge-graph-substrate (the Layer-4 declared-edge surface that this artifact populates), false-positive-dismissal-ledger (dismissals can cite contract-id as scope rather than file:line, surviving file moves), docs-to-code-dependency-graph (this is the directed-authoritative band of the same graph, generalised from docs to subsystem contracts), system-coherence-drift-detector (drift between contract.version and the code that should conform is a concrete coherence signal).

summary:
Calibration experiment complete (2026-05-19). v1 aggressive normalization scored 63.6% on an 11-sample manifest (6 semantic, 5 cosmetic). All 6 semantic samples passed (TP=6, FN=0). 4 of 5 cosmetic samples failed: 3 of those failures were in-function imports being lifted to module scope, 1 was a Retailer→Site class-reference rename (ADR 0012 Phase 1).

Tuning round 1: added in-function Import / ImportFrom node stripping. The rationale is that an import line inside a function body is a way to obtain a symbol (typically deferred for cycle-breaking), not part of the function's observable behavior. The function's behavior depends on what symbols it references, not on how it imports them. visit_Import / visit_ImportFrom return None when the renamer is inside any function scope (self._stack non-empty), and the body iteration filters Nones before re-attaching to the parent.

v2 retest: 90.91% on the same manifest (10/11 match). All 6 semantic samples still pass. 4 of 5 cosmetic samples now pass. The remaining failure (identify_retailer_from_url across e79bf9c3) is the Retailer→Site class rename case: my v1 preserves module-level names, so the AST still differs even though behavior is identical. This is documented in the module header as a known v1 limitation; tuning it would require concepts.yaml integration (rewrite names via superseded_by chain before normalization), deferred to a follow-up.

Operational implication of the limitation: dismissals attached to a function whose class-references get renamed will resurface after the rename. That is arguably correct — reviewers want to re-confirm those dismissals against the new class anyway. In contrast, dismissals against functions where only local variables, docstrings, comments, or whitespace changed will stay dismissed; and dismissals against functions whose semantics changed (added branch, changed constant, modified logic, drop unused in-body import) will reflect the change.

Confidence caveat: 11-sample manifest is small. Will expand during dogfooding (Track 3 fix-now dismissals count toward the n=10 stretch goal by end of Week 2). If real-traffic dismissals show resurface rate exceeding the calibration's 9% miss rate by a large margin, revisit the normalization rules.

summary: Surfaced 2026-05-19 in host-a maintainability lean cut Track 3 (10-findings-and-dispositions.md finding #1). title: /audit-project-shape — two-lens project-shape audit (concept-frequency + recursive layered summary)
origin: host-a session 2026-05-19/05-20: user asked "does summary-of-summaries-of-docs naturally surface project shape?" Two sub-agents answered: one did concept-frequency aggregation across ~45 curated docs (Stage 1 inventory → Stage 2 concept extraction → Stage 3 synthesis → Stage 4 gap report); the other did TRUE recursive layered summarization (Layer A per-doc summaries → Layer B clusters of summaries → Layer C meta-summary on B). Lens 1 surfaced naming hygiene + 5 implicit primitives. Lens 2 surfaced voice/stance drift, directory-vs-topical mismatch, and compression-survival ordering (claims that survive A→B→C are the project's durable shape). Outputs: `.claude/tasks/project-shape-audit.md` + `.claude/tasks/project-shape-audit-recursive.md`. The two lenses are COMPLEMENTARY, not redundant.
summary:
A SUSPECT-tier skill that audits whether a project's curated docs (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md trigger table + the docs they reference + CONTEXT.md + ADRs + concepts.yaml) coherently surface project shape. Two lenses run in parallel:

**Lens A — concept-frequency aggregation** (frequency-weighted cross-doc): Stage 1 inventories every curated doc with its purpose and key claims; Stage 2 extracts noun/verb concepts weighted by cross-doc occurrence; Stage 3 builds hierarchical synthesis (Layer 0 single-paragraph → Layer 1 subsystem clusters → Layer 2 individual docs → Layer 3 supporting refs); Stage 4 produces a gap report (orphan refs, definition drift, dead docs, implicit skeleton candidates, hidden depth, surprising overlap).

**Lens B — recursive layered summarization** (intent / stance / compression survival): Layer A produces per-doc summaries (intent + key claim + stance); Layer B clusters Layer-A summaries by topical affinity (NOT directory) into 6-10 clusters; Layer C produces a single-paragraph meta-summary derived only from Layer B. Stage 4 compares: what survived A→B→C unchanged (durable shape), what lost in A→B (cluster-internal detail), what appeared only at A (specialist content). Stage 5 produces read/skim/skip recommendations.

**Delta**: Lens A is the lens for naming hygiene + vocabulary drift. Lens B is the lens for intent, voice/stance drift, and compression survival. Running both together is significantly higher-leverage than either alone — they catch different drift classes. Concrete evidence from host-a 2026-05-20:
- Lens A surfaced 5 implicit primitives + naming drift in `extraction_code` verb usage.
- Lens B surfaced (1) stale `/README.md` against ADR 0011/0012, (2) voice/stance drift in `site-intelligence-sidecar.md` (filename "sidecar" vs body "main AI runtime"), (3) directory-vs-topical mismatch that the trigger table implicitly compensates for. Lens A missed (1)-(3); Lens B missed the primitives.

**Outputs**: two artifact files under `.claude/tasks/` (`project-shape-audit.md` + `project-shape-audit-recursive.md`) plus a consolidated `project-shape-findings.md` with a triaged fix-now / log-later / monitor disposition table.

**Skill spec**: SUSPECT tier (audit, not action). Default reads `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `<root>/CONTEXT.md` (case-sensitive globbing) + everything they reference via Markdown links + `.claude/contracts/concepts.yaml` if present + `ai-docs/decisions/*.md`. Excludes lazy-loaded skill helpers and task notes by default. Configurable `--include`, `--exclude`, `--lens` (a | b | both, default both).

**When to run**: post-major-refactor sanity check, before a CLAUDE.md restructure, when onboarding velocity drops, when /find-concept-divergence surfaces vocabulary drift, or as a quarterly hygiene pass.

**Composability**: feeds findings into `.claude/quality/findings.jsonl` as `reviewed` records; flagged implicit primitives become `promote-primitive-<slug>` intakes in the LOCAL ledger (not engineering-skills-2 — primitives are project-specific). Lens-A concept inventory can be diffed across runs to detect new drift. Pairs tightly with /find-concept-divergence (canonical names) and find-rule-surface-drift (file-level reachability).
hypothesis:
Two-lens audit will catch ≥1 drift class per project per quarter that single-lens audits miss. The recursive-summary lens is specifically valuable for projects with rich docs (≥20 curated files) where prose drift accumulates faster than concept-name drift. Smaller projects (≤10 curated docs) can run Lens A only.

Validation across 3 projects:
1. host-a (45+ curated docs): both lenses produce non-trivial findings; ≥3 findings unique to each lens; user judges audit ROI as "worth running quarterly". CONFIRMED 2026-05-20.
2. engineering-skills-2 (lighter doc set): Lens A useful, Lens B may be over-engineered. Predicted but unvalidated.
3. A third adopter project: confirms generalizability beyond host-a's specific doc shape.

Counter-hypothesis: recursive-layered summarization is just concept-frequency aggregation with extra steps. Falsified by host-a evidence (Lens B surfaced ≥3 findings Lens A missed, and vice versa). The mechanism is different: Lens A weights by cross-doc occurrence (good for vocabulary), Lens B preserves intent at each layer transition (good for stance drift).

title: Connectors between AI agents working on shared codebases (CLAUDE/Codex/Augment/...)
origin: host-a handoff-prep session 2026-05-20: structural cleanup + navigation-tier READMEs + maintenance tooling bundled together ahead of handoff to an Augment-using maintainer. Plan file at .claude/tasks/handoff-prep-plan.md. Tooling enhancements in Phase 0 surfaced these portable lessons.
summary:
Cross-tool agent setups (Claude Code, Codex, Augment, Cursor, etc.) currently bridge via ad-hoc rule mirroring — `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is the canonical source; `.augment/rules/imported/*.md` is a hand-maintained mirror; `AGENTS.md` is a symlink. This works but is brittle: every rule update requires hand-syncing three surfaces, and drift accumulates silently.

**Backlog**: design a portable 'agent connector' framework that treats the canonical-source + mirror pattern as a first-class abstraction. Properties of the design:

- **Canonical source declared** (e.g. `.claude/` chosen by the project) with mirrors specified as derived artifacts.
- **Sync direction declared** (canonical → mirror, not bidirectional).
- **Mirror drift detection** built in (the host-a `find-augment-mirror-drift` skill is the prototype for one such detector).
- **Mode-specific overrides**: rules that ONLY apply to one tool (e.g. Claude-Code-Specific blocks in CLAUDE.md) declared via structured markers; non-canonical tools skip them.
- **Skill portability layer**: skills written to be tool-agnostic (read from a 'skill manifest' that resolves tool-specific paths) can run on any agent.
- **Memory/context pointers**: agent personal memory (Claude memory, Codex memory, Augment context) shares pointers to durable project guidance without duplicating the content.

**Concrete prototype**: the cross-tool-agent-governance pattern already documented in `.claude/docs/cross-tool-agent-governance.md` is the start; what's missing is the executable substrate (lint, sync tooling, manifest format).

**Adoption path**: start with rule-mirror-drift detection (already in Phase 0 of host-a handoff prep). Expand to a skill manifest format once two projects need it. Full framework lands only when ≥3 projects independently want it.
hypothesis:
A formalized agent-connector framework will reduce per-project rule-mirroring tax from ~10 min per rule update to <1 min, and will let skills built for one agent run on others without rewriting prompts.

Counter-hypothesis: every project's agent setup is too bespoke for a portable framework to work — projects diverge faster than abstractions can keep up. Falsified by evidence if ≥2 projects adopt the same connector format and reduce duplication ≥50%.

Validation across 3 projects:
1. host-a: Phase 0 builds the prototype detector + sync pattern; if mirror-drift detection demonstrably reduces tax, promote to framework intent. Predicted but unvalidated.
2. engineering-skills-2: if itself adopts the pattern for its own CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/Augment-mirror story, second data point.
3. A third project as the cross-cutting validation.

title: tests/ mirror — fixture-path migration for the 14 Path(__file__) tests held back from Phase 1A
origin: host-a handoff-prep Phase 1A (2026-05-20): the 'tests/ mirror app/' move shipped 89 of 103 planned files. 14 use Path(__file__).parent[.parent]* to resolve fixtures relative to the test file, which is the ADR 0015 failure mode in microcosm — moving them would break the fixture lookup. The lean cut left them at tests/ root and logged this intake so a follow-up phase can finish the mirror without re-discovering the failure. Plan file at .claude/tasks/handoff-prep-plan.md; per-file rationale in .claude/tasks/handoff-prep-phase1a-mirror-plan.md.
summary:
**Held-back files (14, all at `tests/` root post-Phase-1A):**

```
tests/test_agent_bridge.py
tests/test_discovery_quality.py
tests/test_field_spec_consolidation.py
tests/test_partshare_quality.py
tests/test_settings_surface.py
tests/test_site_intelligence_apply.py
tests/test_site_intelligence_architecture.py
tests/test_site_intelligence_discovery.py
tests/test_site_intelligence_extraction_validation.py
tests/test_site_intelligence_field_chat.py
tests/test_site_intelligence_snapshots.py
tests/test_site_intelligence_workflows.py
tests/test_site_routes.py
tests/test_visual_extraction.py
```

**Target placement** (per the original mirror plan):

- 8 → `tests/ai/site_intelligence/`
- 2 → `tests/api/`
- 3 → `tests/services/extraction/`
- 1 → `tests/site_management/`

**Why they were held back**

Each uses `Path(__file__).parent.parent / 'testing' / 'fixtures' / ...` (or similar relative traversal) to find fixture assets. Moving the file to a subfolder changes `parent.parent` from repo root to `tests/` (or to `tests/<subfolder>/`), and the fixture lookup fails at import or at first test. This is the same class of breakage ADR 0015 names — asset paths anchored to `__file__` don't survive code moves.

**The companion fix already shipped in Phase 1A**

`tests/tasks/test_sample_download_candidates.py` had `sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(__file__)))`. Post-move the resolution added `tests/` to `sys.path`, which let `tests/scripts/` shadow the top-level `scripts/` namespace package and broke `tests/test_site_intelligence_architecture.py`'s `from scripts.lint import …`. Fix: add one more `os.path.dirname` to anchor to repo root. This was the canary that exposed the broader failure mode and motivated the scope-shrink.

**Three approaches for the follow-up phase**

1. **Project-root anchor via search-up** — compute repo root by walking parents until `pyproject.toml` is found. Robust; no Django dependency; works from any depth. Add a `tests/_helpers/repo_root.py` and have all 14 import it.
2. **Django `settings.BASE_DIR`** — pin to the framework. Cleanest when Django setup has run by the time fixtures load (which is true for these tests). One-line substitution per file.
3. **Move fixtures with the test** — relocate the per-test fixture subtree under `tests/<subfolder>/fixtures/` so `__file__`-relative lookup keeps working. Higher disruption — `testing/fixtures/` is shared by many adapters.

Recommended: option 1 for portability + option 2 as a one-line fallback where the test is already Django-bound. Option 3 only for fixtures that are truly test-local (not shared with `testing/`).

**Pin-test pattern (the ADR 0015 guardrail to apply at move time)**

Before moving each file, add a tiny test that asserts the fixture is still reachable — e.g. `assertTrue(FIXTURE_DIR.exists())`. With the anchor switched, the pin-test passes before AND after the move, proving the anchor change is invariant. This is what Phase 1A skipped (because the 14 files weren't yet flagged as a class) and what the follow-up should not skip.
hypothesis:
If a follow-up phase applies one of the three anchor approaches (project-root search-up, `settings.BASE_DIR`, or test-local fixture relocation) plus the pin-test gate, all 14 files can move to their planned `tests/<subfolder>/` targets without regressing the 2426-test baseline. The work is ~150-200 LOC of edits + 14 pin-tests + a small shared helper.

Validation: post-follow-up, the full `tests/` suite still reports 2426 tests / 8 baseline failures (or fewer if the holds happen to fix latent issues). `find-broken-file-refs` reports 0 delta. The always-suite stays at 92/92.

Counter-hypothesis: 'leave them at tests/ root forever — the mirror is asymmetric but functional.' Falsified by the cost during Phase 2 README writing — the 14 root-level tests confuse the tests/<subfolder>/README.md coverage statements and force the Phase 2 author to write 'plus N orphan files at root' caveats in multiple READMEs. The cost of leaving them at root accumulates every time someone scans the test layout.

Adding three surface-specific write-time prompts (service: decompose; view: check layer; new method: grep verb+noun first) to agent posture docs will reduce fresh layer-violation findings on new views and fresh cross-file semantic-duplication findings, without regressing the omnibus discipline which is already modal in services. Validation: re-run the four detection skills on a host project N weeks after posture-doc adoption; expect proportionally fewer findings on freshly-written code (filtered by git log recency). Falsification: if fresh-code findings rates are unchanged, the discipline is being skipped or the prompts aren't surface-routed correctly.
summary: Write-time named-function decomposition is widely treated as the universal discipline for AI-generated code health, but retrospective evidence from a mature codebase suggests it is only one of three distinct levers — and which lever applies depends on the surface being written. (1) Service-layer decomposition (role-naming inside one file) is already the modal practice in well-tended codebases; the residual concern is borderline 2-domain bleed at >1000 LOC. (2) View-layer awareness ('only HTTP-layer logic in HTTP entry points, never business logic') is underused; the lever is layer-choice before writing, not decomposition during writing — this is the highest-leverage write-time intervention because it prevents fat-view violations at source. (3) Cross-file discovery before writing ('grep for verb+noun in the same package before adding a new method') is the only effective intervention for semantic duplication, because decomposition cannot see across files. Proposed: extend agent posture docs (e.g. senior-engineer-posture.md) with three surface-specific prompts rather than a generic 'decompose into named functions' rule. Case study — host-a 2026-05 retrospective: /find-omnibus 0/10 confirmed (8 FP because decomposition already in place); /find-layer-violation 8/8 fat-view findings on one views file (decomposition would not have moved logic to the right layer); /find-duplication ~20% within-file vs ~80% cross-file; /find-semantic-duplication 100% cross-method parallel-growth across files. Composability: relates to senior-engineer-posture doc lineage and architectural-smells layer-violation; potentially feeds a /pre-write-check or surface-aware write-time prompt loader.

Reframe: name outward-facing quality as a SECOND axis with five faces (security, resilience, observability [application + product], data/privacy, cost/abuse), tracked with a two-tier model — FLOOR = find-standard-gaps ast/grep standards (deterministic, coverage-checked, always-on) + CEILING = kind:manual standards owned by the role-based review-avatar lane so the declared baseline stays complete. Shipped so far: standards.example.json expanded 2→14 grouped by dimension; senior-engineer-posture.md §4 + the .augment mirrors (both repos); ADR 0018 (proposed). Pairs with ADR 0019 (external-content trust boundaries) for the AI-specific security half.

title: Project-lifecycle-stage core: a user-facing reasoning layer that stage-gates which standards are active and flags when a project crosses a maturity line
summary: The single biggest real-world hole: transitioning prototype -> production and FORGETTING to upgrade standards. Reframe (from user): the gap is rarely missing model KNOWLEDGE — general training already covers production standards (idempotency, fail-closed, default-deny, retention, races). It is ACTIVATION: 'hit the goal somehow' mode + standards inherited from whatever the surrounding (often vibe-coded) project already tolerates suppresses them. So standards are not binary; they are STAGE-GATED, and the most-skipped move in software is noticing you crossed a line and re-deciding the bar. The core: (1) establishes & maintains the project's stage — driven by ORIENTATION QUESTIONS asked of the user, because the agent cannot infer stage from code alone (real users or test data? internal or about-to-be-public? blast radius?); (2) maps stage -> active standards (floor/ceiling entries gain a `min_stage` gate); (3) detects transitions and surfaces 'you crossed into stage X; these N standards just became relevant; here is the current gap'; (4) is user-facing (asks + reports). Proposed stage vocab: 0 prototype/spike (only meta-standard: mark-it-a-prototype so it can't graduate silently); 1 first-real-users/data (input validation, fail-closed on irreversible paths, secrets hygiene, authz default-closed, structured logging, reversible migrations); 2 production (idempotency, observability/correlation, resource+cost bounds, data lifecycle/PII, kill switches, compatible contracts); 3 scale/multi-tenant/regulated (concurrency/races, object-level authz, backpressure/SLOs, threat modeling, compliance). Open design forks: stage granularity (global vs per-area vs hybrid); transition trigger model (pull /orient vs push-on-signals vs both). Turns ADR 0018's one-line 'staged to maturity' into the actual mechanism.
hypothesis: A stage-aware activation layer prevents the most common real-world failure — silent graduation from prototype to production without re-deciding standards. Validation: on a project that crosses a line (e.g. adds first real users / a public deploy / an unauth write endpoint), the core flags the newly-relevant tier and the floor/ceiling gap, and the user confirms or corrects the stage call.

hypothesis: Converting prose obligations into declared-evidence + procedure-in-code yields proof that is both noise-robust and model-portable; LLM verification is a stakes-gated supplement, not the baseline.
summary: Distinct axis from static artifact coherence (IAC bands / skill_meta lint / smokes): does an agent actually DO a skill's steps and honor its constraints when running it against real-world noise? Authoring checks (/plan-skill) + dogfooding prove a skill CAN run faithfully once; they don't guarantee faithful execution every time. Noise failure modes: step-skipping, premature 'good enough', constraint-dropping (silently violating a not_for/guard), quiet abandonment. Harness strength ladder (weak->strong): self-reported checklist < independent LLM verifier-pass (post-hoc, adversarial) < declared-evidence enforcement (deterministic: did produces/evidence_required artifacts materialize, shaped right?) < procedure-in-code (the step IS a script the runner sequences). Hinge: produces/evidence_required is already TYPED in skill_meta but dormant (~8/66 skills) -- same field serves both lanes: Band A checks declared+well-formed, the harness checks delivered-at-runtime. v1: deterministic declared-evidence enforcement, opt-in + coverage ratchet (3rd use of the block-on-declared/ratchet pattern after smokes + frontmatter contract); stakes-gated LLM verifier-pass for no-artifact constraint-drops (ADR 0020 activation). CROSS-MODEL CONSTRAINT (user 2026-05-22): different LLMs execute skills differently, so the harness needed to prove performance differs by model. This splits the ladder by portability -- deterministic rungs (evidence, procedure-in-code) are MODEL-AGNOSTIC (the only portable proof); LLM rungs are MODEL-COUPLED (pin a fixed strong verifier, never self-grade; per-model thresholds). Implications: skills should declare a validated-on execution floor; behavioral dogfooding must be a multi-model replay matrix (script-smokes already model-agnostic); writing a skill to its WEAKEST target executor (more code, less prose-trust) raises BOTH the cross-model floor and noise robustness with one lever -- noise and cross-model collapse into the same fix; harness depth ladders on stakes x executor-tier; the multi-model matrix doubles as a model-robustness benchmark (which skills are safe to delegate to cheap models). OPEN FORK: make produces/evidence_required load-bearing (promote + ratchet -- leaning this, a declared evidence contract is what makes the proof portable) vs opt-in. Defer: full orchestration (resilient-agent-architecture).
title: Skill runtime-adherence harness (evidence-enforcement + stakes-gated verifier, cross-model-aware)

summary: Cross-model reframed (user): the multi-model dimension is primarily an ABLATION tool, not a support-validation matrix -- vary the executor to test whether each check/scaffold you built actually earns its keep (no model needs it=cut; all need it=harden into code; only weak models need it=model-tier scaffolding). "A check's existence != its necessity." Dependency that sequences the work: ablation presupposes a deterministic, model-agnostic success oracle, so the evidence-harness v1 is its prerequisite -- build the oracle first, THEN ablate. Procedure-in-code sharpened by the for-loop test: the LLM must never be the system-of-record for completeness or iteration count -- code owns the loop + completeness ledger, the LLM owns per-item judgment (mechanical loop = pure code; agentic loop = LLM drives each step but code still tracks coverage + partitions failures, per the resilient-agent pattern). Tradeoff named: guarantee vs flexibility, paid in upfront specification. Status: open research aspiration, not a build task.

Agentic-primitive refinement (user): an LLM in an agentic shell (tool-calling runtime) outperforms a bare one, so "push control flow into code" must NOT mean taking the loop away from the agent -- that kills the agency where the performance lives. Resolution: keep the agent driving, but give it an easy-to-call orchestration PRIMITIVE that holds the completeness guarantee. Determinism moves INTO a callable tool, not OUT of the agent; the right slogan is "completeness lives in a primitive the agent calls," not "procedure-in-code." Splits the harness into two postures that reinforce: inline primitive (proactive -- a for-each/task-ledger tool the agent calls so it can't lose the count; TodoWrite is an existing instance) + post-hoc gate (reactive -- evidence check that all N happened). The gate can police primitive-USAGE ("10-item step, agent never called the orchestration tool"), not just outcomes. Two constraints: (1) ergonomics are load-bearing -- if the primitive is clunkier than winging it, the agent routes around it, so it must be the path of least resistance; (2) the failure mode MOVES not vanishes -- from "tracked the loop badly" to "forgot to use the loop tool" (still progress: calling a tool right is easier than a mental ledger). Folds into ablation: which primitives a skill needs is model-tier-dependent + ablatable (strong model iterates 10 fine without a for-each tool; weak one needs it). Unifies the threads: agency makes the model perform -> requires callable primitives -> whose per-tier necessity is found by ablation -> existing to move completeness out of the LLM's head. Status: research aspiration.

The three refinements (runtime adherence -> cross-model ablation -> agentic primitives) now live there as §1-2 scope/criteria, §5 the harness strength ladder + primitive/gate duality + ablation-needs-oracle ordering, §6 open forks (load-bearing produces/evidence_required; first orchestration primitive; verifier rung). summary: Owner vision refinement (2026-05-25), tying this intake to the "React-like one-way data flow from docs to code" idea the owner wants to build but hasn't yet. The heart is two diff-driven operations. (1) FORWARD: a doc/decision diff determines the downstream change-set — code is a projection of many upstream constraints, so changing a constraint marks its dependents dirty. This is the React re-render intuition but invalidate-and-flag, NOT regenerate — consistent with this intake's existing "relation not a function" stance: the graph propagates typed dirtiness and proposes; it cannot re-render code. (2) REVERSE: given a code execution/region, enumerate every decision/lens/assumption that shaped it (reverse index over the same edges). Owner flags REVERSE as the key unmet capability ("knowing what all the decisions/lenses that impacted a given code execution actually are") and it is arguably higher-value for an agent about to touch code than forward propagation. Assumes all changes originate upstream as doc/source changes. STORAGE FORK left open: owner has always thought it needs a graph DB; prior suggestion was JSON/JSONL-as-graph stored in git. Direction to explore — separate query model from storage: graph query model yes, graph-DB storage only as a derived cache if scale ever demands; git-native edge files projected into an in-memory graph keep the source co-versioned with the repo, which is the whole point of a docs-to-code graph (a separate DB just recreates doc-rot at the graph layer). First shipped edge / concrete grounding: host-a ADR 0018 + read-decode-safety.v1's new assumes/revisit_when fields (2026-05-25, both repos) are one hand-authored upstream(assumption)->downstream(decision) edge with manual dirtiness. ~6 implicit edge sources already exist scattered: ADR applies_to, precedent applies_to/guards/revisit_when, decisions.py link-check, Python imports, concepts.yaml aliases. Passive v0 = harvest these into one queryable place + mark dirty + show blast radius. Owner status calibration: "don't think we're very far in building that system out" — stays state:proposed; this is vision refinement plus one shipped micro-instance, not a build.

hypothesis: Editing the authoritative requirement doc as a reviewed constraint delta BEFORE coding yields better-constrained implementations than spec-alongside planning, and is the front door of the diff-reactive change loop (the doc edit is the upstream diff the docs-to-code graph would propagate). Adversarial review of the PLAN -- not merely producing a plan -- is what surfaces decisions otherwise made silently.
origin: 2026-05-25 diff-reactive change-loop dialogue (docs->code one-way dataflow); user: 'we don't have and haven't tried a make-change skill'
summary: A change starts as an edit to the authoritative requirement doc, not a parallel spec. Sequence: (1) locate the authoritative doc for the area (the CLAUDE.md trigger->doc table + concepts.yaml already aid 'find the right doc'); (2) make a clearly-defined, nuanced, suitably-constrained change to that doc AND the requirements it represents -- a constraint delta, not just edited prose; (3) draft a plan, then run an adversarial review ON THE PLAN to surface the decisions/questions worth deciding before coding (the technique /plan-skill already uses for new skills); (4) implement guided by the updated doc. Distinguishing premise (one-way docs->code dataflow): every existing planning skill READS docs and WRITES a NEW parallel spec (plan-feature -> ai-docs/specs/, scope/impact/plan-spec); NONE edits the authoritative doc as the primary action, so changes silently fork doc from spec (the parallel-writer / format-equivalence smell). Dogfood evidence: which-skill routes 'change how X works' weakly to /plan-feature (score 7) with no clean home. Forks for maturation: (a) standalone skill vs doc-first MODE on /plan-feature; (b) which doc-classes are 'authoritative' (CLAUDE.md docs, ADRs, CONTEXT.md/concepts.yaml, ai-docs/specs).
title: make-change: doc-first change skill -- find the authoritative doc, edit it as a constraint delta, adversarially review the plan, then implement from the updated doc

hypothesis: A two-commit speed bump (deactivate the guard in a solo, greppable commit before changing the protected target) converts accidental decision-wrecking into a deliberate, reviewable act without locking out motivated change.
origin: 2026-05-25 skill-ecosystem self-review (host-a). The F1 near-miss: a SUSPECT-style read of skill frontmatter flagged the deliberately read-only EXPLAIN job as mislabeled, and a fix-now authorization nearly relabeled it. Skills have no traditional tests protecting intent.
summary: Skills have no traditional tests protecting their INTENT, so a confident agent can "fix" a deliberate design decision and pass every artifact/routing check (exhibit A: the F1 near-miss relabeling the read-only EXPLAIN job). The guard: register the triple {why-record, guard, protected-target} in a manifest; a TARGET-SIDE pre-commit/CI hook blocks any commit that changes a protected target while its guard row is still active. The only way through is a prior SOLO commit that deactivates the manifest row and touches nothing else -- which auto-enforces "remove the guard first" ordering without the hook reasoning across commits, and keeps detection structural (a manifest-row diff) rather than a fragile is-this-test-weakened analysis. It is a speed bump, not a vault: --no-verify and manifest edits exist, matching the sufficiently-motivated clause -- the override is just forced to be standalone, greppable, and reviewable. Generalizes beyond skills: the same tripwire protects any load-bearing invariant in host code (cannot delete the test for X and change X in one commit), so it is a candidate pattern, not a one-off. The manifest IS the machine-readable Record-to-Guard link, making the verify-intent control (the dogfooding-controls path for working in a skill system) concrete. Pairs with the skill-design-rationale precedent entries (the Record leg) and skill-ecosystem-quality-gate (where cheap invariants like extract-or-propose implies job=explain live as assertions).
title: unguard-first guard: a load-bearing decision guard cannot be weakened in the same commit that changes the protected target; un-registering it must be a solo commit first

hypothesis: The conceptual system is slow due to three taxes (redundant analysis, routing/reading tax, round-trip-per-finding execution); compiling to analyze-once plus decide-once plus batch-execute removes all three, while the conceptual version remains the legible source you reason about and protect.
origin: 2026-05-25 design dialogue (host-a). The prod vision: 1. do lots of analysis, 2. create one big plan to transform the project to a healthier state, 3. execute. Motivated by the current piecemeal system being "super slow".
summary: The current skill ecosystem is a CONCEPTUAL/SOURCE form: many small separated skills (map-suspect-explain-refactor-guard as discrete stages, 4 distinct duplication detectors, EXPLAIN-propose separate from REFACTOR-execute) optimized for legibility, protectability, and conceptual integrity (= the VISION legibility destination). The PROD regime is different: (1) lots of analysis, (2) ONE global plan to transform the project to a healthier state, (3) batch execute. Thesis: the conceptual version is the SOURCE; the prod version is a COMPILED BUILD of it -- derive the fast one from the legible one rather than choosing between them (like a readable codebase vs its minified bundle). The speed win removes three taxes of the source form: redundant analysis (4 dup- plus ~13 drift-detectors each re-parse the tree, so analyze ONCE into a shared model and detectors become queries), routing-plus-reading tax (N skills / N reports / N human decisions; which-skill cannot even route the planning cluster, so decide ONCE over the whole graph), and round-trip-per-finding execution (so batch it). CRUCIAL: the prod version is only trustable because it removes the human-in-the-loop the source form leaned on per stage, and what replaces that judgment is the why-records plus guards plus unguard-first tripwire. So the build order is guards/why, then substrate, then planner, then batch-executor (also the safest order: batch execution scales blast radius, so guards must be load-bearing first). Already latent across four intakes nobody has composed: code-knowledge-graph-substrate (step 1), target-architecture-artifact plus propose-architecture-skill (step 2 / Shape B), plan-phased-refactor-skill (step 3). skill-execution-planner is the closest precursor (a scheduler over the skill graph) but this adds the source/build two-regime model and the guards-first prerequisite. Hard parts: global planning must sequence dependent refactors (map before extract; fix refs before moving folders) and stay coherent as execution changes the code under the plan (the staleness/fixpoint problem, hence Shape B as a target plus re-derivation).
title: Conceptual-source to prod-build: compile the legible multi-skill system into a single analyze-plan-execute pipeline for speed (guards-first)

ES2 custom AST lints all reuse ruff noqa grammar for suppressions: silent_catch.py, no_bare_delay.py, no_fat_view.py, no_comment_drift.py, no_stringly_typed_status.py, and codegen_emits_new_paths.py each define a NOQA_RE matching '# noqa: <code>: <reason>', where <code> is a lowercase-hyphenated project name (safe-dispatch, silent-catch, fat-view, comment-drift, stringly-status, codegen-emits-new-paths). ES2 also runs ruff (pyproject.toml + CI) and sets neither external nor RUF100. Ruff lexes the token after 'noqa:' as one of its own rule codes (uppercase + digits like F401); a lowercase-hyphenated name cannot lex, so ruff emits a cosmetic 'Invalid # noqa directive' warning on a cold cache whenever such a line also carries a real ruff finding. Proven in the sibling host-a repo that the bare form warns identically with and without ruff external, so external cannot fix it. Fix: give project lints their own allow-marker such as '# lint-allow: <code>: <reason>', update each lint NOQA_RE, migrate the existing directives, and update the lint docs. Value: removes the cosmetic warning across all project lints, decouples custom lints from the ruff namespace, and unblocks enabling RUF100 later; cross-cutting, so ADR-scope rather than ad-hoc. Surfaced via cross-project propagation from a host-a guard-hardening investigation; evidence here is re-derived from ES2 own lint scripts and ruff config (no host-a refs carried over). Relates to standards-floor-detector-refinements item 3 but is distinct: that teaches a detector to READ noqa as a human-judgement signal, whereas this moves project lints OFF the ruff noqa namespace, so a coordinated change would also teach that floor the new marker.
title: Migrate custom-AST-lint suppressions off ruff noqa namespace to a dedicated marker

hypothesis: A ratchet over structural metrics catches the integral-scoped rot (omnibus accretion) that diff-scoped guards structurally cannot see.

title: Structural seatbelt — ratcheting baseline over structural metrics (LOC, fan-in, responsibility count), not just lint rules

The baseline file becomes a machine-readable backlog with an assigned drainer — draining it IS the batch sweep, so the GUARD artifact and the sweep work queue unify. From the Atlas probe (their HEAD commit was literally 'Auto-tighten eslint-seatbelt baseline'; the missing half is the agent that drains it).
title: Ratchet baselines invert under agents: from permanent amnesty to drainable work queue

hypothesis: Folder/module conventions that include a token-cost band prevent both monolith accretion and coordination-overhead fragmentation.

There is an interior optimum set by working-set token cost. ADR 0006 gates folder packaging on sibling COUNT; an AI-first convention also gates module size — and the Atlas probe showed a placement rule without a granularity rule (non-UI goes in src/libs) manufactures omnibus modules. Candidate amendment to ADR 0006 and input to ADR 0034 W2 de-flavoring.
title: Optimal module-size band set by context-window economics — placement conventions need granularity rules

title: One typed registry file per cross-cutting surface — the highest retrieval-value-per-token artifact

title: Generated structural indexes are the missing third context tier at scale

title: High-bar refusal rules for entropy surfaces — do_not_do_next as standing policy
